correctness.rationale: Using Qin’s assumed positive unique fixed-point limit m for all finite connected graphs, dividing m_e=m_e^α Σ_{v∈e}q_v/D_v(m) by m_e^α gives Br=m^(1−α), r_v=q_v/D_v(m)>0. Conversely every positive solution r of Br=s corresponds to q_v=r_vD_v(m) and the same unique equilibrium. Connected unsigned incidence has kernel zero iff graph has an odd cycle; otherwise it has one alternating sign vector and positivity produces exactly an open interval of inverse rates. For uniform q_i=p on C_n, differentiating the equilibrium yields the cyclic positive definite L=(1-α/2)I+(α/4)(shift+inverse shift), eigenvalues 1−α sin²(πk/n)>0; input derivative p(h_i+h_{i+1})/2 gives multiplier p(1+e^{iθ})/[2(1−α sin²(θ/2))]. Maximizing absolute mode gains yields threshold α_n, continuum envelope and finite-n endpoint limits. Positive alternate q=p(1+ε(-1)^i) has exactly constant m_i=p on even rings. Independent graph incidence ranks and Fourier norm checks corroborate. Crucial external existence/uniqueness premise is attributed to Qin, not proven from source here.
